**Project Summary: Nairobi Youth Code Initiative**

The Nairobi Youth Code Initiative will equip 240 secondary school students across four partner schools with practical digital skills, opening pathways to higher education, employment, and entrepreneurship. Kenya's growing technology sector offers real opportunity, yet many young people in Nairobi's under-resourced neighborhoods lack access to computers, qualified instructors, and structured learning.

Over two years, the program will deliver a progressive curriculum covering web development, Python programming, and problem-solving. Each school will host weekly after-school sessions led by trained facilitators, supported by a dedicated computer lab. Students will complete hands-on projects addressing community challenges, and top performers will receive mentorship and internship placements with local technology partners. We will prioritize participation by girls, targeting at least 50 percent enrollment.

The total budget is KES 6.2 million, covering equipment, facilitator training and stipends, curriculum materials, connectivity, mentorship, and evaluation. This works out to roughly KES 25,800 per student. Success will be measured through skills assessments, project portfolios, retention rates, and post-program tracking of education and employment outcomes.
